cases.title: Finch: conversational finance data agent in Slack
cases.problem: Finance analysts lose time locating datasets and writing complex SQL; requests to data science take hours or days.
cases.depth: Detailed architecture with evaluation approach; no quantitative results published
technologies_stated: Slack SDK and Slack AI Assistant APIs
Uber Generative AI Gateway (self-hosted and third-party LLMs)
facts: The agent runs inside Slack using the Slack SDK and AI Assistant APIs, with live status updates.
SRC-023
LangGraph coordinates a supervisor that routes requests to specialised sub-agents such as a SQL writer and a document reader.
SRC-023
Models are reached through an internal generative AI gateway so they can be swapped; both self-hosted and third-party LLMs are used.
SRC-023
Data is exposed as curated single-table data marts; an OpenSearch index holds column names, values and aliases for fuzzy matching of filter values.
SRC-023
The SQL writer checks the user's permissions before running a query; RBAC limits access to sensitive financial data.
SRC-023
Evaluation compares query results against golden queries, tests supervisor routing on ambiguous intents, runs end-to-end simulations and regression re-runs before prompt or model changes.
SRC-023
Sub-agents run in parallel and common metrics are pre-fetched to cut latency.
SRC-023
The authors acknowledge hallucination risk and plan on-demand expert validation of answers.
SRC-023
interpretations: Comparing result sets rather than SQL text tolerates equivalent queries but needs stable reference data; it can mask semantic mistakes when both queries share the same wrong filter.
I
Simplifying schemas into single-table marts moves complexity from the model into data engineering, trading flexibility for reliability.
I
unknown: Quantified accuracy, latency, adoption or time savings
How RBAC is implemented and how identity reaches the data sources

decisions.alternatives: Expose the raw warehouse and let the model plan joins; semantic layer or metrics store; pre-built dashboards only
decisions.reasoning: Source states the aim is lower query complexity and faster retrieval. Alternative trade-offs are independent analysis.
decisions.basis: documented rationale; alternatives are independent analysis

decisions.selected: Supervisor routing to specialised sub-agents in LangGraph
decisions.alternatives: Single agent with all tools; fixed workflow with intent classifier; fully autonomous planner
decisions.reasoning: Source documents the supervisor design and tests routing accuracy. Why not the alternatives is not stated.
decisions.basis: documented design; alternatives are independent analysis

decisions.selected: Internal gateway so models can be swapped
decisions.alternatives: Direct provider SDKs per agent
decisions.reasoning: Source states swappability. Broader lock-in reasoning is independent analysis.

decisions.selected: Search index with aliases for fuzzy matching
decisions.alternatives: Model guesses literal values; exact match only; user picks from list
decisions.reasoning: Source describes the index purpose. Failure modes of alternatives are independent analysis.

decisions.selected: Golden-result comparison plus routing, end-to-end and regression tests
decisions.alternatives: Manual spot checks; LLM-as-judge only; production feedback only
decisions.reasoning: Source describes the suite; no explanation of rejected approaches.

cases.review_exercise: Finch states permission checks occur before query execution but not how identity propagates. List three ways a delegated agent could exceed a user's data rights and the control that closes each.
lessons: Constrain the data the model sees before tuning the model.
Evaluate agents per component and end to end, and regression-test before every prompt or model change.
Plan human validation for decisions that matter, because the authors themselves cite hallucination risk.
cases.adaptation: For SAP CX analytics (sales or service KPIs), the same pattern maps to BDC data products as the curated layer and Joule Studio or a BTP agent as the supervisor; identity propagation then becomes the main design question (see T2.4.2). This mapping is independent analysis.

cases.title: Genie: enhanced agentic RAG over policy documents
cases.problem: An on-call Slack copilot answered security and privacy questions inaccurately over 40+ policy documents; a golden set of 100+ expert questions showed answers were incomplete or wrong.
cases.depth: Detailed pipeline and evaluation method; relative improvements only
facts: A custom Google Docs loader replaced PDF parsing because standard PDF loaders lost table structure and no single parser worked across documents.
SRC-024
An LLM converts tables and structured text to markdown; table chunks are kept intact via metadata; documents get LLM summaries and chunks get FAQs and keywords.
SRC-024
Pre-retrieval agents rewrite ambiguous queries, split complex ones into sub-queries and identify the most likely source documents.
SRC-024
Retrieval runs vector search and BM25 over enriched metadata and merges results as a union; a post-processor deduplicates and orders chunks by position in the source.
SRC-024
Evaluation uses expert reference answers run in batch with an LLM judge scoring 0-5, cutting evaluation turnaround from weeks to minutes.
SRC-024
Reported results are relative: 27% more acceptable answers and 60% fewer incorrect answers.
SRC-024
interpretations: Changing the source format (Google Docs instead of PDF) was a bigger lever than changing the model, which is a common ingestion lesson.
I
Relative gains without baselines cannot be converted to absolute quality; ask for the baseline before quoting these numbers to a client.
I

decisions.selected: Custom Google Docs loader with table-aware markdown conversion
decisions.alternatives: Keep PDF parsers (several tried); OCR or layout models; re-author sources
decisions.reasoning: Source documents PDF parsers losing table row and column context and no universal parser.

decisions.selected: Hybrid vector plus BM25 union over enriched metadata
decisions.alternatives: Vector only; BM25 only; reranker-based fusion
decisions.reasoning: Source describes the hybrid; the choice of union over reranking is not explained.

decisions.selected: Query optimizer and source identifier agents before retrieval
decisions.alternatives: Single-pass retrieval with raw query
decisions.reasoning: Source describes the agents as handling ambiguity and narrowing sources.

decisions.selected: Expert references plus LLM judge with reasoning
decisions.alternatives: Human review per release; synthetic questions only
decisions.reasoning: Source cites speed gain. Judge validity is not reported.

cases.review_exercise: The reported 60% reduction in incorrect advice has no baseline. Define the evidence you would request, and how you would test the judge's agreement with experts before trusting it.
lessons: Fix ingestion before tuning generation.
Enrich chunks and queries; do not rely on raw similarity alone.
Judge-based evaluation speeds iteration but must be validated against humans.
cases.adaptation: For an SAP service knowledge assistant over product manuals and notes, the same ingestion-first approach applies; the access-control question (not answered in the source) must be designed explicitly. Independent analysis.

cases.title: Dash: RAG plus code-planned agents for universal business search
cases.problem: Business knowledge is scattered across apps, formats and modalities, slowing search and raising access-control risk.

technologies_stated: LLM-planned code in a Python-like DSL
facts: Dropbox chose a traditional lexical index with embedding-based reranking over a pure vector index.
SRC-025
For complex tasks an LLM expresses a plan as code in a Python-like DSL which a purpose-built minimal interpreter validates with static analysis and dry runs.
SRC-025
The interpreter implements only required functionality to reduce the risks of a full-featured interpreter.
SRC-025
The post names trade-offs: latency versus quality, freshness versus scalability, budget versus experience, model size versus latency and accuracy.
SRC-025
Evaluation uses public datasets plus LLM judges for correctness and completeness and passage-level precision, recall and F1.
SRC-025
The post reports over 95% of queries completing in 1-2 seconds.
SRC-025
Prompts do not transfer cleanly between models.
SRC-025
interpretations: Planning as code makes failures locatable and testable, giving determinism that free-form tool loops lack.

unknown: Model names, embedding model, index technology
How permissions are enforced inside retrieval and agent execution

decisions.selected: Lexical index with embedding reranking
decisions.alternatives: Pure vector index; pure lexical search
decisions.reasoning: Source states these as trade-offs; detailed reasoning is limited.

decisions.selected: LLM-written code in a restricted DSL executed by a custom interpreter
decisions.alternatives: Iterative tool calling; general-purpose Python sandbox; fixed workflows
decisions.reasoning: Source describes the DSL approach and its security benefit of a minimal interpreter; alternatives comparison is independent analysis.

decisions.alternatives: Live API calls per query; full real-time indexing
decisions.reasoning: Source discusses the freshness versus scalability trade-off.

Make retrieval model-agnostic and measure it end to end.
State trade-offs explicitly to clients.

cases.title: Dash: knowledge graphs, MCP limits and DSPy
cases.problem: Scaling an AI search product exposed context bloat, latency in MCP-based agents and unmanageable prompts.
cases.depth: Candid lessons and rejected alternatives; few quantitative results
technologies_stated: LLM-as-judge (an OpenAI o3 upgrade is mentioned)
facts: Tool definitions and returned content consume context; Dropbox caps context at about 100,000 tokens because quality degrades beyond it.
SRC-026
Some MCP-based agents took up to 45 seconds for a simple query versus seconds with direct index access.
SRC-026
Mitigations include one 'super tool' over the index instead of many retrieval tools, storing large results outside the model context and sub-agents with narrower tool sets.
SRC-026

A graph database was tried and rejected for latency, query pattern and hybrid retrieval reasons; graphs are built asynchronously and compressed into bundles that go through the normal chunk and embed pipeline.
SRC-026
Index-based retrieval was chosen over federated retrieval for connector coverage, preprocessing and speed, at the cost of engineering effort, storage and freshness management.
SRC-026
DSPy is used to optimise prompts against evals, starting with judge prompts; about 30 prompts are edited by 5-15 engineers.
SRC-026
interpretations: Federated MCP access is attractive for speed of integration but shifts quality and latency to each external system.
I
unknown: Knowledge graph schema and bundle construction

decisions.selected: Central index
decisions.alternatives: Federated retrieval via MCP connectors to each app
decisions.reasoning: Source lists connector access, preprocessing, offline ranking and speed in favour of the index, and cost and freshness against.

decisions.selected: Single super tool over the index
decisions.alternatives: 5-10 separate retrieval tools
decisions.reasoning: Source cites context cost and tool selection quality.

decisions.selected: Graph summarised into bundles in the existing retrieval pipeline
decisions.alternatives: Dedicated graph database
decisions.reasoning: Source states graph database was rejected for latency, query pattern and hybrid retrieval difficulty.

decisions.selected: Programmatic optimisation with DSPy
decisions.alternatives: Hand-edited prompt strings
decisions.reasoning: Source states preference for generating prompts from goals.

cases.title: Intent Engine: LLM-driven query understanding with teacher-student distillation
cases.problem: Legacy query understanding struggled with broad queries, noisy labels, tail queries and fragmented models; rewrites covered about half of search traffic.
cases.depth: Detailed architecture, latency engineering and metrics; teacher model unnamed
facts: Strategy: start from LLMs and inject company context via RAG, validate with guardrails, then fine-tune.
SRC-027
An offline teacher pipeline with caching handles head queries and produces training data; a smaller fine-tuned student serves tail queries in real time.
SRC-027
Out-of-the-box latency was close to 700 ms on A100; merging LoRA adapters and moving to H100 reached about 300 ms.
SRC-027
FP8 quantisation cut latency roughly 10% but reduced recall, so unquantised serving was chosen.
SRC-027
Caching means only about 2% of queries need real-time inference.
SRC-027
Reported results include rewrite coverage above 95% with precision above 90%, and a 50% drop in complaints about poor tail-query results.
SRC-027
interpretations: Splitting offline quality from online latency is the key architectural idea: spend frontier-model cost where latency does not matter, distil for where it does.
I

decisions.selected: Offline large-model teacher plus distilled small student
decisions.alternatives: Call a frontier model online for every query; classical models only
decisions.reasoning: Source cites latency and cost constraints at search scale.

decisions.selected: Taxonomy-bound guardrails with similarity thresholds
decisions.alternatives: Trust model output; human review of all outputs
decisions.reasoning: Source describes the validation layer.

decisions.selected: Keep unquantised
decisions.alternatives: FP8 quantisation
decisions.reasoning: Source states a recall loss outweighed ~10% latency gain.

cases.review_exercise: The post cites a 30% latency gain in one place while its numbers imply a bigger change. How would you reconcile before presenting this to a client?

Fine-tuning is for behaviour and consistency here, with RAG supplying knowledge.
Make quality trade-offs measurable.
cases.adaptation: Relevant to SAP Commerce search and B2B catalogue query understanding. Independent analysis.

cases.title: Slack AI: privacy-first generative AI architecture
cases.problem: Deliver generative AI features while keeping customer data inside the trust boundary and honouring existing compliance commitments.
cases.depth: Detailed on security and hosting decisions; no quality or latency metrics
technologies_stated: Closed-source LLMs hosted in an AWS escrow VPC
facts: Four principles: customer data stays in the trust boundary, no training on customer data, AI only shows what the user can already see, and enterprise security and compliance still apply.
SRC-028
Closed-source models run in an escrow VPC on AWS so the model provider has no access to customer data.
SRC-028
Slack chose off-the-shelf models with RAG over fine-tuning on customer data because it could not guarantee sufficient protections.
SRC-028
Retrieval uses the requesting user's access control lists and existing display libraries; output is visible only to the requester.
SRC-028
Outputs are ephemeral and not written to disk; stored data follows a least-data principle and existing key management and residency infrastructure.
SRC-028
If a source message is removed by DLP, derived summaries are invalidated.
SRC-028
interpretations: Reusing existing authorisation code paths for retrieval is a strong pattern: the AI layer inherits, rather than reimplements, access control.
I
unknown: Technical detail of the escrow VPC
Prompt construction and evaluation (deferred by the authors)

decisions.selected: Provider models inside an escrow VPC
decisions.alternatives: Hosted provider API; self-hosted open model; vendor-managed private deployment
decisions.reasoning: Source documents data-ownership requirement and that vendors generally do not ship closed models for self-hosting.

decisions.selected: RAG with stateless model calls
decisions.alternatives: Fine-tune on customer data
decisions.reasoning: Source states it could not guarantee strong enough protection if training on customer data.

decisions.selected: Requesting user's ACLs at retrieval
decisions.alternatives: Service-level access with output filtering
decisions.reasoning: Source states AI must show only what the user can already see.

cases.review_exercise: Derived summaries are invalidated when a source message is deleted. Identify two other places an AI system might retain derivatives of deleted data and how to detect them.

Inherit authorisation from the system of record.
Stateless RAG simplifies privacy arguments.
cases.adaptation: Maps directly to SAP CX client conversations about data residency and no-training terms with Generative AI Hub. Independent analysis.
